api_safety.backward_compatibility: Adds causative/applicative/neuter/passive analysis and generation under height harmony. Under morphology-rules-v3 the analyzer also returns exact-lemma and homograph ambiguity as multiple analyses (exact reading first), generation metadata lists this card when these extensions are applied, and evidence-gated allomorphs (dz, ts; short reversive) are refused with 422 EXTENSION_UNVERIFIED (see the retained card).

High-vowel radical with mid-vowel causative surface violates height harmony; the analyzer returns 422.
-urur-/-oror- surfaces are the repetitive extension (own card), not causative/applicative/passive/neuter stacking.

notes: This card authorizes passive (-w- / -ew- / -iw-), causative (2) (-is- / -es-), applicative (-ir- / -er-) and neuter (-ik- / -ek-) under height harmony.
Causative (1) -idz-/-edz- and -its-/-ets- shapes are evidence-gated: generation refuses them with 422 EXTENSION_UNVERIFIED (see the retained card for the locators found and still missing).

Multi-extension stacks follow the documented sequence convention (at most three, each type once, canonical order causative < applicative < reciprocal < reversive < repetitive < neuter < passive). Fortune states the constructional pattern 'R + extension(s)' without an ordering rule, and attested combination radicals appear in section 3.4.2.8 (e.g. -pamhidz-ir-an-, PDF p. 110 / printed p. 98), so the convention is a conservative product limit shared by generator and analyzer, not a claimed grammar rule.
Causative (2) -is- and intensive -is- share one surface; the analyzer reports the causative reading and meaning disambiguation stays lexical.
Perfective (-irir-) and extensive (-ik-) are source-noted but not implemented as extension types; -ik- surfaces analyze as neuter.
Reciprocal -an- is documented in its own evidence-backed card (fortune.verbal.reciprocal.001).

qa.reviewer_notes: Locator corrected from the unverified 1955 Analytical Grammar citation to the inspected local source: Fortune Vol. 1 (1985), section 2.10.2.3.3, PDF p. 33 (printed p. 21), including the -eC- footnote. Examples separate source-attested radicals from constructed combinations.

rule_summary: Passive (-w- / -ew- / -iw-), causative (2) (-is- / -es-), applicative (-ir- / -er-) and neuter (-ik- / -ek-) verb stem extensions under height harmony: -iC- after /a/, /i/, /u/ or C radicals, -eC- after /e/ or /o/.
source_locator: Fortune, Shona Grammatical Constructions Vol. 1 (1985), section 2.10.2.3.3 'Extended radicals', PDF p. 33 (printed p. 21), paragraphs (a) and (d) plus the -eC- footnote
title: Core verb extensions under height harmony
